1,

The present petition has been filed under Section 528 of BNSS for quashing of FIR No.24 dated 17.01.2020, registered at Police Station Division No.8, Police Commissionerate Ludhiana, District Ludhiana, under Section 174-A IPC.
2.

sentences.text:
Learned counsel contends that FIR No.322 dated 10.11.2018, under Section 420 IPC, Section 24 of the Immigration Act and Section 13 of the Punjab Prevention of Human Smuggling Act, 2012,
registered at Police Station Division No.8, Ludhiana, was registered against the petitioner.

entities.text: Punjab Prevention of Human Smuggling Act, 2012
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: He could not appear before the trial Court due to his involvement in other cases whereupon he has wrongly been declared proclaimed person, vide order dated 20.11.2019, Annexure P-1, since mandatory provision of Section 82 Cr.P.C. has not been complied with, consequent to which present FIR was registered under Section 174-A IPC.

During the interregnum, compromise was arrived at between the parties and on the basis thereof, the FIR No.322 dated 10.11.2018 was quashed by this Court,
vide order dated 07.04.2025.
Thus, the submission CRM-M-21147-2025 made is that continuation of the present proceedings would amount to abuse of process of Court.

Reliance is placed on Karuna Bhardwaj vs. State of Punjab and another, CRM-M No. 39164 of 2023, decided on 15.11.2023 and Devinder Sharma vs. State of Punjab, CRM No. 39058 of 2021 in CRM-M 3489 of 2020 decided on 24.11.2021 Lovely Kumar vs State Of Punjab on 6 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/114036592/

sentences.text: 3. Learned State counsel submits that the FIR was rightly registered as the petitioner was declared proclaimed offender by the trial Court for having absented.

4. Heard.
5.

Pertinently, vide order dated 07.04.2025 passed by this Court, whereby FIR No.322 dated 10.11.2018 was quashed, based on compromise and affirmed by statement recorded before the learned trial Court which gave a report to that effect.

6. In similar set of facts and circumstances, while placing reliance on the judgments of Devinder Sharma vs. State of Punjab CRM-M-18146-2011 dated 05.07.2011; Jitender Singh vs. State of Haryana CRM-M-47891-2021 dated 16.11.202; Microqual Techno Limited vs. State of Haryana,
2015(32)RCR (Criminal) 790, the proceedings initiated under Section 174-A IPC, were quashed by this Court in the case of Karuna Bhardwaj (supra), wherein FIR registered under Sections 406, 420,
448, 465, 467, 471, 474 & 120B IPC had been quashed on the basis of compromise, by observing therein that, "Having considered the respective arguments raised by the learned counsel for the parties, this Court finds substance in the arguments raised by counsel for the petitioner.

sentences.text: The objective of the coercive mechanism prescribed under the Code of Criminal Procedure is to ensure that the person PARVEEN KUMAR 2025.11.07 17:55 + : .

[attest to the accuracy andemains present before the Court to receive the order or the sentence, if any, so integrity of this order/judgment.
PARVEEN KUMAR 2025.11.07 17:55 CRM-M-21147-2025 awarded by the trial court to such a person.
However, in the present case, the FIR in question stand quashed.

Since, the said offence itself has been wiped out, therefore, the petitioner would not be required to face any other proceedings in which the court could have awarded any punishment or pass any other order qua the petitioner."

7. In the present case, the petitioner was declared a proclaimed offender on 20.11.2019, pursuant to which the impugned FIR was registered on 17.01.2020, however, FIR No.322 dated 10.11.2018 stands quashed on 07.04.2025, hence this Court finding that continuation with the proceedings in question would amount to an abuse of the process of the Court, thus, in light of the judgment in Karuna Bhardwaj (supra), the FIR is liable to be quashed, in exercise of power under Section 482 Cr.P.C.
8.

Considering the aforesaid facts and circumstances of the case and the decisions referred, this Court finds that the continuation of proceedings against the petitioner pursuant to FIR in question,
would be an abuse of process of law.

Accordingly, the present petition is allowed and FIR No.24 dated 17.01.2020, registered at Police Station Division No.8, Police Commissionerate Ludhiana,
District Ludhiana, under Section 174-A IPC, is quashed.
